newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed, follow late Dow slide.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed, follow late Dow slide.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks ended mixed on Tuesday after a volatile session * TSE rallied early on U.S. data, but followed late Dow slide * 134 million shares traded worth C$2.1 billion
Toronto stocks ended mixed on Tuesday, surrendering most of its early gains following a late slide in New York.
The TSE 300 Index rose 5.95 points to close at 6046.71 in brisk turnover of 134 million shares worth C$2.1 billion.

But declining stocks outpaced advances 498 to 468 with 320 issues unchanged. Canadian equities jumped early with Wall Street after an unexpectedly subdued fourth quarter employment cost report. "Intially the reaction to the data was strong, but now it's falling back a bit," said Ira Katzin, an investment advisor wth RBC Dominion Securities.
The U.S. data sent equity and bond markets higher earlier today, but it also prompted a sell-off in gold markets. COMEX February gold finished down US$3.30 at US$354 an ounce.
The TSE's precious metals fell 48 points, leading seven of 14 sub-groups lower. Other weak sectors included communications, base metals and conglomerates.
The strong side was led by energy, forestry products and utilities.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Northern Telecom Ltd rose 1.60 to 93.90 after announcing plans to buy back up to 4.0 million shares.
U.S. investment house Goldman Sachs also raised Northern to market outperform from market perform on Tuesday.

* Gulf Canada Resources Ltd gained 0.50 to close at 11.60 after hitting a 52-week high of 12.25. Gulf Canada locked horns with Britain's Clyde Petroleum on Tuesday as they argued over the fairness of Gulf's offer.

* Pure Gold Resources topped heavy traders, adding 0.075 to 0.31 on 9.04 million shares after Ashton Mining of Canada said that the first two holes in a program of drilling in north central Alberta intersected kimberlitic rocks.
